moatVerdict: A narrow moat in automotive glass (scale, OEM approvals, a shareholder-customer), none in clear float glass. Returns on capital (ROCE 11-12% in FY25-26) have not covered a ~12% cost of capital through the last investment cycle.
critiques: Returns are low for the capital used: ROCE fell from 21% (FY22-23) to 11-12% (FY25-26) after Rs2,835 cr of capex in FY24-26; the chairman himself says 'the next phase must be about ... higher returns', yet another Rs2,000 cr is approved.
Float profits depend on trade protection: the Aug-2026 minimum import price lasts one year; FY22-23 showed what high import prices do (34% margin) and FY24-25 what imports do when they fall (18-20%).
Maruti is customer and promoter: Rs873 cr of sales in FY26 and approval for up to Rs1,500 cr in FY27 (30% of turnover) are related-party transactions; Maruti's bargaining power caps auto margins.
Equity dilution: the Rs1,000 cr QIP (Sep-2025) added 4.9% to the share count; FY26 EPS fell 9% (Rs13.82 vs Rs15.27) even as profit before dilution was flat.
Q1FY27 looks like a peak: auto margins benefited from in-house float glass and record car volumes; the GST-boosted base arrives in Q3FY27.
Bull case (ICICI Securities): float capacity ramp-up and value-added auto glass drive double-digit EBIT growth; 22x FY28E EV/EBITDA.
governance: 10 directors, 3 women; CMD Sanjay Labroo is a promoter and his relative Nisheeta Labroo a non-executive director; Maruti nominates a non-executive director (Shashank Srivastava); a Japanese whole-time director (Masao Fukami, 33 years in automotive glass) and a non-executive Japanese director (Kazuo Ninomiya, replacing an AGC retiree)
